mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has risen steadily from -3.4 to 2.0 over the past four weeks, indicating commuting routines are resuming. This sustained increase in workplace mobility will continue to lift retail-and-recreation footfall as more people move through commercial zones during weekday commutes, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -3.4 to 2.0 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days does not increase relative to the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise at least 2 points per week.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility sustains above 7.5% for two consecutive weeks, it signals renewed use of public transport for shopping and leisure trips, which will drive a short-term increase in RETAIL_REC over the following 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains above 7.5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at 7.7% in t-0w, above 7.5% threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the 2 weeks following two consecutive weeks of TRANSIT above 7.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in WORKPLACES (from -3.4 to 2.0) and decline in RESIDENTIAL (from 8.6 to 5.1) jointly indicate a behavioral shift away from home-centric routines toward out-of-home economic activity. Together these compounding trends will push RETAIL_REC higher over the next 4 weeks more strongly than either series alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rising AND RESIDENTIAL falling concurrently for 3 or more weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES up 5.4pts while RESIDENTIAL down 3.5pts over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines despite continued joint WORKPLACES increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined from -11.7 to -12.6 over four weeks, consistent with worsening winter air quality and cold weather in Delhi that discourages outdoor activity. This seasonal substitution effect will push consumers toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -11.7 to -12.6 over 4 weeks
regime_hint: winter post-monsoon air quality season in Delhi
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise despite continued PARKS decline during the winter season, or PARKS decline reverses with seasonal warming without a corresponding RETAIL_REC drop.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in WORKPLACES mobility, crossing from negative to positive, signals formal relaxation of work-from-home mandates. If WORKPLACES sustains above 2% for two weeks, this policy-driven return-to-office will increase weekday retail traffic near commercial hubs, raising RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES sustains above 2% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES crossed from -3.4 to +2.0 over 4 weeks, turning positive in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the 2 weeks after WORKPLACES sustains above 2%, or WORKPLACES reverses below 0% due to renewed restrictions.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has plateaued near 13-15% with a slight pullback from 15.4 to 14.1, suggesting essential-goods demand is saturated. Limited household budgets reallocate spending toward groceries and pharmacy rather than discretionary retail and recreation, keeping RETAIL_REC flat or lower over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 15.4 to 14.1 in the most recent week while RETAIL_REC stayed near -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next week despite continued plateau or decline in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility peaked at 8.7% in t-1w then fell to 7.7% in t-0w. If this week-on-week decline exceeds 1 point and continues, it signals waning willingness to travel for non-essential trips, which will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 1 point week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from 8.7 to 7.7 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next week even though TRANSIT continues to decline by more than 1 point per week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen steadily from 8.6% to 5.1% over four weeks. If it drops below 4% for two consecutive weeks, this threshold crossing indicates substantial easing of stay-at-home policy pressure, which will drive increased RETAIL_REC over the following 2 weeks as residents resume out-of-home discretionary trips.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 8.6 to 5.1 over 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the 2 weeks following RESIDENTIAL falling below 4%, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 6%.
